cost.note: Metered = what the harness recorded per run. Distinct parses = every unique request text ever sent, which also covers runs that were interrupted before writing a meta file. The campaign total adds the variability repeats back on top of the distinct-parse figure and is rounded up.

stages: UPLOAD A FOREIGN GPX (lon-first attrs, rtept, extra junk)

distance.why: The product's own acceptance band: routes/scoring.py rejects any candidate more than 15% from the target, so 15% is the promise being tested, not a number chosen to flatter the result. Edits use 18% because an edit re-routes around fixed endpoints and has less freedom to hit a length exactly.

loop_closure_m.why: routes/editing._is_loop uses 250 m. Wider than it looks: a loop that starts and ends on opposite sides of a divided road is closed for a rider.

start_proximity_m.why: Geocoding a landmark returns a building centroid; the router snaps to the nearest routable way. 600 m absorbs both without hiding a route that starts in the wrong place.

via_m.why: BRouterProvider.VIA_NEAR_M -- the app's own definition of 'the route goes through there'. A town is an area, and forcing the geocoded centroid creates touch-and-retreat tendrils. Tightened per-case to 1500 m for a specific landmark.

avoid_on_road_m.why: Measured as meters ridden within 28 m of the named road's real OSM centerline (the same measure routes/road_avoid.py uses to verify an avoid edit). Under 200 m is a crossing or a forced first/last block, not riding the road.

teleport.default: gap > 800 m AND a bearing change of 60 deg or more
teleport.why: A first attempt used a plain 600 m gap threshold and flagged three perfectly good routes: Wisconsin's section-line grid gives dead-straight mile-long roads, which BRouter emits as a single segment. Requiring the long segment to ALSO turn away from the route's heading keeps the check able to catch a real splice without punishing straight rural geometry. Recorded here because the threshold was wrong before it was right.

repeat_frac.why: routes/scoring.py rejects loops above 25% repeated road. Reported for every route; only enforced on loops, because an out-and-back is 100% repeated BY DESIGN and flagging that would be a scorer bug, not a product bug.

climb_cap_slack.why: A stated ceiling is a hard promise: routes/scoring.py rejects anything above it, so the eval does too, with no slack. The elevation figure itself carries roughly +/-10% instrument spread (see PROVENANCE), which is reported alongside.

provenance.geometry: BRouter 1.7.10, self-hosted, profile fastbike-quiet, OSM extract tiles W90_N40 / W95_N40 (southern Wisconsin).
provenance.elevation: SRTM-derived elevations carried in BRouter's GeoJSON output. The app's climb figure is routes/elevation.track_ascent, a model calibrated against RideWithGPS and one barometric .fit file; the devlog records that instruments themselves disagree by 8-16%, so +/-10% is the attainable accuracy. The eval reports the app's number AND an unsmoothed independent sum over the same elevations. Neither is ground truth -- only a barometric ride is.
provenance.geocoding: OSM Nominatim, public endpoint, no key.
provenance.road_geometry: OSM Overpass API, way centerlines, used for the avoid-road measurement.
provenance.not_measured: Whether a route is SAFE or PLEASANT to ride. No check in this harness establishes that. Traffic volume, shoulder width, pavement quality, sightlines and seasonal conditions are outside what OSM tags and this eval can see. Those claims would need field riding.
